'''Ilya Kapovich''' is a Russian-American mathematician and a [[Professor]] of [[Mathematics]] at the [[Hunter College]] of the [[City University of New York]]. He is known for his contributions to [[geometric group theory]], [[geometric topology]], and [[Computational complexity|complexity theory]].

==Career==
He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from the [[Graduate Center of the City University of New York]] in 1996 under the direction of [[Gilbert Baumslag]].<ref name="Ilya Kapovich">{{MathGenealogy|id=35543}}</ref> After postdoc positions at [[Rutgers University]] and [[Hebrew University]], he worked at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] from 2000 to 2018.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Kapovich|first=Ilya|date=|title=CV|url=http://math.hunter.cuny.edu/ilyakapo/cv1.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-20|website=}}</ref> While at Illinois, he has had several visiting positions. Most notably, he was an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] research fellow at [[Frankfurt University]] during Spring 2006, and Ada Peluso Visiting Professor at [[Hunter College]] during Spring 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Mathematics and Statistics Faculty at Hunter College|url=http://146.95.100.32/faculty.shtml#visiting/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-27|website=146.95.100.32}}</ref> 

==Recognition==
In 2012, he was named an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. He delivered an invited address at 2008 Spring Eastern Sectional meeting of the AMS.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=AMS 2008 Spring Eastern Sectional Meeting Invited Addresses|url=https://www.ams.org/meetings/sectional/2149_invited.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-20|website=}}</ref>

==Contributions==
He has worked on problems related to automorphisms of free groups, free-by-cyclic groups, mapping class groups as well as complexity and decision problems in group theory. He has supervised 9 PhD students to completion as of 2022.<ref name="Ilya Kapovich">{{MathGenealogy|id=35543}}</ref> 

Between 2010 and 2015, he served on the editorial board of the [[LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics|LMS Journal of Mathematics and Computation]].<ref name=":0" /> 

His older brother [[Michael Kapovich]] was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Davis]], and his twin brother [[Vitali Kapovitch]] is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Toronto]]. <ref>{{Cite web|last=Kapovich|first=Misha|date=|title=Misha Kapovich's bio|url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~kapovich/bio.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>
